title: Presynaptic homeostasis mediated by exocytosis of a SNARE protein
title_zh: 由SNARE蛋白胞吐介导的突触前稳态
abstract: The neural plasticity that underlies adaptation and learning requires countervailing homeostatic mechanisms to maintain the stability and responsiveness of neural circuits. Previous work has described several forms of synaptic homeostasis1, but the mechanisms that detect changes in activity and transduce these into altered neurotransmission have remained poorly understood. Here we show that high-frequency stimulation alters the subsequent properties of neurotransmitter release to confer a presynaptic form of homeostasis, independent of postsynaptic receptors. The mechanism involves vesicular SNARE protein (v-SNARE) VAMP7 (vesicle-associated membrane protein 7), which reduces neurotransmitter release by inhibiting the entry of Ca2+ specifically through P/Q-type presynaptic Ca2+ channels. Previous work has implicated target SNARE proteins (t-SNAREs) in the inhibition of Ca2+ channels2, but without clear physiological rationale. We show that the activity-dependent regulation of release mediated by VAMP7 requires the t-SNARE syntaxin. Although VAMP7 acts at the plasma membrane to inhibit P/Q-type channels, it localizes predominantly to a subset of synaptic vesicles made by adaptor protein-3 (AP-3) that respond specifically to high-frequency stimulation3,4. The localization of VAMP7 to AP-3-derived synaptic vesicles thus provides a mechanism for the activity-dependent delivery of VAMP7 to the plasma membrane, where it associates with syntaxin to inhibit P/Q-type Ca2+ channels and transmitter release. This homeostatic form of metaplasticity operates at multiple excitatory synapses, and in its absence, the fraction of FOS+ neurons increases several fold, revealing a general property of excitatory neurotransmission that might also maintain the sparsity of neural connections. Experiments show that when subjected to high-frequency stimulation, excitatory neurons exhibit a presynaptic form of homeostatic plasticity mediated by the exocytosis of v-SNARE protein VAMP7 and the resulting inhibition of P/Q-type calcium channels.
abstract_zh: 支撑适应与学习的神经可塑性需要对抗性的稳态机制，以维持神经回路的稳定性与响应性。先前的研究已描述了多种形式的突触稳态1，但检测活动变化并将其转化为改变神经传递的机制仍不甚清楚。本文表明，高频刺激会改变随后神经递质释放的特性，从而赋予一种独立于突触后受体的突触前稳态形式。该机制涉及囊泡SNARE蛋白（v-SNARE）VAMP7（囊泡相关膜蛋白7），其通过特异性抑制P/Q型突触前Ca2+通道的钙流入来降低神经递质释放。先前的工作曾将靶SNARE蛋白（t-SNARE）与Ca2+通道的抑制联系起来2，但缺乏明确的生理依据。我们表明，VAMP7介导的活动依赖性释放调节需要t-SNARE语法素。尽管VAMP7在质膜处作用以抑制P/Q型通道，但其主要定位于由适配蛋白-3（AP-3）生成且专门响应高频刺激3,4的一小群突触小泡中。VAMP7定位于AP-3源性突触小泡，从而提供了一种活动依赖性将VAMP7递送至质膜的机制，在那里它与语法素结合以抑制P/Q型Ca2+通道和递质释放。这种稳态型前体可塑性在多个兴奋性突触上起作用，且在其缺失时，FOS+神经元的比例会增加数倍，揭示了兴奋性神经传递的一般性质，可能也有助于维持神经连接的稀疏性。实验表明，当受到高频刺激时，兴奋性神经元表现出由v-SNARE蛋白VAMP7胞吐及其引起的P/Q型钙通道抑制所介导的一种突触前稳态可塑性形式。
